questions.stem: Your wake tips a canoe near a dock. Who is responsible for the harm it causes?
options: The canoeist, for paddling too close
No one, because wakes are natural
The marina that owns the dock
You, the operator making the wake
questions.explanation: The operator is responsible for damage or injury caused by their wake.

questions.stem: On a BC lake, what is the speed limit within 30 m of shore for a power boat?
options: 5 km/h
20 km/h
10 km/h
15 km/h
questions.explanation: The VORR set 10 km/h within 30 m of shore on BC rivers and lakes, posted or not.

questions.stem: You are 20 m off a beach in Desolation Sound, on the coast, with no posted limit. Does the 10 km/h shoreline rule apply?
options: Yes, it covers every BC shoreline
No, in BC it is lakes and rivers
Yes, but only in July and August
No, it applies only where posted
questions.explanation: In BC the 10 km/h within 30 m rule covers rivers and lakes, not coastal waters. Still use a safe speed.

questions.stem: Which regulations list the local no-motor, speed and towing-hour limits for named lakes?
options: Vessel Pollution and Dangerous Chemicals Regulations
Marine Mammal Regulations
Competency of Operators of Pleasure Craft Regulations
Vessel Operation Restriction Regulations
questions.explanation: Local restrictions are set by the VORR and listed by water body in its schedules.

questions.stem: Your cruiser has a toilet and you boat on Okanagan Lake. What must you do with the sewage?
options: Hold it and use a pump-out on shore
Pump it overboard in deep water
Pump it out at night, away from beaches
Add chemicals, then empty it in the lake
questions.explanation: Untreated sewage must never go into a lake or river. Okanagan Lake is also a designated sewage area.

questions.stem: On the BC coast, outside any designated sewage area, where may a small pleasure craft discharge untreated sewage?
options: Anywhere the water is over 20 m deep
Only inside a sheltered harbour
At least 3 nm from shore, under way
At least 1 nm from shore, at anchor
questions.explanation: Untreated sewage may go overboard only 3 nautical miles or more from shore while the boat is under way.

questions.stem: You notice an oily film in the bilge. What should you do?
options: Pump it overboard right away
Add bilge cleaner and pump it out
Wait for the wake to wash it clean
Soak it up with absorbent pads
questions.explanation: Never pump oily water overboard. Bilge cleaners only break oil into small drops.

questions.stem: What should you do with drink cans and food wrappers on a day trip?
options: Bring them back to shore
Sink them in deep water
Throw them over well offshore
Burn them on a beach fire
questions.explanation: Garbage is a pollutant. Bring it all back to shore.

questions.stem: You are trailering from Shuswap Lake to Kalamalka Lake. Which step is part of Clean, Drain, Dry?
options: Rinse the hull in the new lake
Pull the drain plug at the launch
Leave weeds on to dry on the road
Keep live-well water for the bait
questions.explanation: Drain means pulling the plug and emptying the bilge and live well before you leave the launch.

questions.stem: You are driving with a kayak on your roof and pass an open invasive mussel inspection station in BC. What does the law say?
options: Only motor boats need to stop
Stop only if you are leaving BC
Stop only if the kayak is wet
You must stop and report
questions.explanation: Anyone moving a watercraft in BC, including a kayak, must stop at every open inspection station.

questions.stem: A group of Pacific white-sided dolphins is resting near your boat. How far must you stay?
questions.explanation: Whales, dolphins and porpoises need 100 m. If they are resting or with a calf, it is 200 m.

questions.stem: In 2026, how far must boats stay from Southern Resident killer whales in southern BC waters?
questions.explanation: From June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 the distance is 1,000 m. Other killer whales in BC need at least 200 m.

questions.stem: You see a killer whale off Haida Gwaii, far from the southern BC zone. What is the legal minimum distance?
questions.explanation: The Marine Mammal Regulations set 200 m for killer whales in all BC and Pacific waters.
